title: Exactness of finite-level inverse image
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite-dimensional field extension of Q_l in universe u, T and S schemes in universe t, and g : T → S. Use the positive-index coefficient sheaves O_E/(l)^(n+1), their specified quotient maps, and the coefficient tower categories and normalized equivalences of det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian. For every n : ℕ, the left adjoint of the ordinary module direct image spLevelPush(l,E,g,n) preserves finite limits. Together with its left-adjoint preservation of colimits, this says that finite-level inverse image is exact.

proof.text: Replace the pro-etale sites by their compatible coefficient-sized AsSmall models. On constant commutative ring sheaves the base-change inverse image is canonically the same constant ring: both composites are left adjoint to sections at the terminal object and its base change. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the transpose of the canonical constant-section map with this isomorphism. Transport it to the model sites.

Commute forgetting ring structure past inverse image and check its unit equation. This gives the ring unit presentation required by inverseImage_underlying_of_ring_presentation. That theorem identifies module inverse image followed by forgetting scalars with abelian inverse image. Abelian inverse image preserves finite limits; the module forgetful functor reflects finite limits. Hence the model module pullback preserves finite limits.

Use the ringed-site module equivalences for AsSmall and the pushforward-composition isomorphisms to identify the transported right adjoint with the specified finite-level direct image. Uniqueness of left adjoints transports preservation of finite limits to its recorded left adjoint. Apply this to the lifted quotient ring at exponent n+1.
